QA REVIEW EVIDENCE + LANDING (the qa_approve summary digests this).

WIRE COMPATIBILITY — the risk this row actually carries. Extracting proof framing means every existing signature breaks if a byte moves, and the committed byte-identity test compares the shared function against a daemon wrapper that just calls it, so it cannot detect a shared-side change. I closed that gap directly: a differential probe reimplementing the DELETED daemon path verbatim from the HEAD blob (readExactRecord then framed, Buffer + writeUInt32BE) versus the new shared canonicalSessionProofBytes produced IDENTICAL bytes on five fixtures — base (324B), unicode incl. a surrogate pair (332B), zero generation/issuedAt (312B), MAX_SAFE_INTEGER issuedAt (327B), 1000-char nonce (1292B) — and refusal PARITY on eight hostile shapes: extra key, missing key, inherited-only property, array, null, getter-backed field, non-enumerable field, symbol key. (My first parity pass showed a false MISMATCH on "extra key" because I had replicated `framed` without the `readExactRecord` gate that precedes it; corrected, both throw.) Separately, the daemon's own session-authority test independently pins the exact domain and thirteen u32be-framed fields, so the wire bytes are pinned on both sides, not only through the wrapper.

GATES RE-RUN BY ME: contracts session-authority-canonical 26/26; daemon session-authority-protocol + session-authority 30/30; client session-key 11/11; focused runtime-provider-control-room.security 9/9; @moe/contracts, @moe/daemon, @moe/control-room-client typechecks and `tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json` all exit 0. Numbers match the worker's report exactly.

THREE INDEPENDENT DRILLS, each red on its named arm, each restore SHA-256 proved:
- Shared proof ORDER (swapped "transportId"/"requestId" in the frozen field list): contracts "pins the full domain plus u32be-framed field-order oracle" red, AND the daemon "pins the exact domain and thirteen u32be-framed challenge fields in order" red. Restore to dd401f92...ad446a4.
- SPKI WIDTH guard loosened (`!== 44` to `> 1024`): security RACE arm red plus the slice's no-admission invariant, and one client unit red. Restore to 33c1662d...cef012c.
- Reinserted a daemon-private `const SESSION_PROOF_DOMAIN`: the structural "contains no daemon-local proof framing or proof-constant definitions" test red. Restore to 8a883b34...b8f1325.
All four legs green again after restore.

STAGING RED, VERIFIED NOT TAKEN ON FAITH: the full lane is 4 files / 20 tests failed. I removed the new sheet (SHA-256 170dcb4ad80beb2cc274e47f43a8a2c70f0ca16f3f9167ce429260c4b57b3e34), re-ran, and got exactly 3 files / 13 tests — the disclosed baseline — then restored it byte-identically. So the 7 added failures are precisely this row's, all in completeness.security.ts under SECURITY_COVERAGE_FOREIGN_BOUNDARY: CONTROL_ROOM_SESSION_KEY, which the approved plan's step 4 authorizes verbatim ("Record, do not hide, that the nonempty SESSION_KEY receipt intentionally remains a full-lane SECURITY_COVERAGE_FOREIGN_BOUNDARY staging red until sibling C and final row task-45839f34 serialize the roster/partition"). I am approving a lane that is redder than before ONLY because the plan ordered that sequencing and the row's rails forbid touching the roster.

RAILS: contracts module has zero runtime `node:`/Buffer use (the only hits are comments saying so). generateSessionKey passes `extractable=false` and returns CryptoKey handles; the security ledger records arm/boundary/caseId metadata only, no key material. BOUNDARY_ROSTER and runtime-provider-invariants.ts untouched. The foreign untracked tests/security/goal-closure-verification-fixture.ts was left alone.

LANDING: commits null with the delivering seat worker-76a8c4ac at IDLE/currentTaskId null 65s after REVIEW — 10th occurrence. Staged the nine owned paths from a provably empty index (never add -A), committed 79315504 (703+/49-), then record_commit. Committed bytes equal the verified tree modulo the repo's `* text=auto eol=lf`. Note for a later row, not this one: packages/contracts/src/index.js remains untracked in the shared tree and is not part of this delivery.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected importing the daemon protocol into browser production or copying its proof canonicalizer: apps/control-room cannot depend on an app package, a copy would create two byte authorities, and the daemon must remain the sole verifier. Rejected moving generic frame/scalar/framed or Node crypto wholesale: sessionReplayDigest still consumes daemon-owned framing, and hashing/SPKI/Ed25519 verification are Node-only. Rejected adding a generateSessionKey dependency parameter or changing its exports: the function already reads global WebCrypto at call time, its throw/non-pair/44-byte guards are present and divergence-testable, and changing the signature would fan out through the root export scanner and E2E callers. Rejected an empty security receipt: the row must prove executed SESSION_KEY arms; the deliberate foreign-boundary full-lane red is serialized to the existing final roster row rather than hidden. No docs file is changed because this is an internal byte-authority extraction with preserved public daemon behavior; focused source comments carry the non-obvious ownership.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured at HEAD 7333327fe568a3622c7e7312f7ecf6a2fe9249d7 with `git status --porcelain=v1 -- <exact ten>` empty. Nine paths exist; only tests/security/runtime-provider-control-room.security.ts is absent. Lines: contracts canonical 68/bridge 1/index 228/test 71; daemon contracts 221/protocol 305/test 85; client session-key 157/test 237. Existing contracts canonicalization and root edge are PRESENT from task-d37e887; this row extends rather than reimplements them. Daemon alone owns local 13-field CHALLENGE_ORDER and proof bytes today; its session-authority test is the run-only full-hex/368-byte oracle. Replay framing shares frame/scalar/framed, so those helpers must stay. Both manifests declare @moe/contracts and lock importers link it; temporary bare imports of sessionAuthorityCanonicalString compiled under @moe/daemon and @moe/control-room-client and were deleted in the same command. Fresh baselines: contracts canonical 1 file/7 tests; daemon protocol+session-authority 2 files/27 tests; client session-key 1 file/9 tests, all exit 0; focused new security file exits 1 with `No test files found`; @moe/contracts, @moe/daemon, @moe/control-room-client and security tsconfig typechecks all exit 0. Parent comments comment-1b0aac3f/comment-70a36aa strike its stale ownership and make it a zero-byte closure. Real production consumer child task-28cd95db8bb6444b861eac4384c7fdc2 depends on this row; sibling C task-87f13cbaa8ee43208810abead90d5744 serially extends the same security file; final roster task-45839f34c88d4db291146bd6f2216b99 depends through that parent closure.
planningNotes.risks: The proof bytes are signature authority: one order, framing, UTF-8-length, integer, or domain drift invalidates persisted/interoperating signatures, so both computed identity and an independent exact hex oracle are required. Do not accidentally remove replay framing when deleting proof duplication. The current SESSION_KEY guards already satisfy the requested behavior; needless source changes add reachability risk, so preserve logic unless a production test first demonstrates a gap. The new runtime-provider file writes a real SESSION_KEY receipt while the master roster/partition are deliberately out of scope; therefore full `pnpm test:security` acquires an expected diff-caused SECURITY_COVERAGE_FOREIGN_BOUNDARY until task-45839f34 lands. This is explicitly authorized by parent comments and must be disclosed, never presented as green. Never serialize/log a key handle; fake sentinel values stay outside ledger payloads. The security file is untracked until created, so restore proof must use an out-of-tree backup and separate SHA-256 comparison. Shared-worktree foreign dirt is not a block and must never be reset/stashed/adopted.
